items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And they had a guy called Max Dreyfus who was famous — I mean he was an accomplished pianist, brilliant musician.

ctx.x: Like a book, exactly. I mean the famous one, I think it was — who was the publishers of the Cole Porter things? Anyway, famous, one of those companies. And they had a guy called Max Dreyfus who was famous — I mean he was an accomplished pianist, brilliant musician. I mean he could spot a well constructed song. He was Jerome Kern’s amanuensis. I mean he was responsible. He brought Gershwin in there, I mean all these people, they really knew quality. But like you say, like book publishing, you had an editor who…
Well I have a very small theory that technology plays a role in this in that the more toys a person has to play with, the less quality you’re going to come up with—
